item.title: San Francisco celebrates Valkyries' historic championship with an all-time parade
item.description: Valkyrie fans celebrate during the parade in San Francisco on Nov. 4, 2026. (Douglas Zimmerman/SFGATE) San Francisco was once again the city of champions as the Golden State Valkyries celebrated the organization's first-ever WNBA title with a parade on Wednesday. Around 400,000 fans wearing some variation of the team's violet and black colors lined up down the Embarcadero in anticipation of seeing their favorite players, who just pulled off a historic accomplishment: the fastest expansion team to win a championship across all major North American professional sports teams. They completed their milestone on Saturday, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in seven hard-fought games. Golden State star Gabby Williams put together an all-time Game 7 performance that enshrined her in the annals of Bay Area sports history and secured a championship that had eluded her throughout her entire career. Gabby Williams looks at fans during the Valkyries' victory parade in San Francisco on Nov. 4, 2026. (Charles Russo/SFGATE) Valkyrie fans celebrate during the victory parade in San Francisco on Nov. 4, 2026. (Douglas Zimmerman/SFGATE) Kaitlyn Chen hands a bottle of champagne to Valkyries fan Sarita Contreras during the parade in San Francisco on Nov. 4, 2026. (Douglas Zimmerman/SFGATE) Fans cheer on Valkyries players during the victory parade in San Francisco on Nov. 4, 2026. (Charles Russo/SFGATE) Now that the basketball was over, the partying could begin. Players reveled in the cheers and chants featuring their respective names while riding violet buses down from Mission Street to right in front of Oracle Park. They sprayed the crowd with champagne, shotgunned beers, chugged bottles of whatever came with them on their bus and even came down to the crowd to celebrate with the people - where they shotgunned more beers . When the barricades ended at the final stop of the parade route, fans mobbed the Valkyries stars that got off the bus with photo requests and thank-you's for what they accomplished. Even with the victory secured four days ago, Wednesday's parade wasn't always expected to go like this. Through most of Tuesday, the weather called for the rain to continue. But as if to say that this day was deserving of some sunshine, the sky opened up, and the sun shined brightly on San Francisco and its newest champions. Fans react to the Valkyries players during the victory parade in San Francisco on Nov. 4, 2026. (Charles Russo/SFGATE) From left, Laeticia Amihere, Veronica Burton and Kaitlyn Chen wave to fans during the victory parade in San Francisco on Nov. 4, 2026. (Charles Russo/SFGATE) The Valkyries team arrives by ferry for the victory parade in San Francisco on Nov. 4, 2026. item.title: Ryle takes top-ranked St. Xavier to the wire in state soccer semifinals
item.description: LEXINGTON, Ky. – Ryle pushed one of the best teams in American to the wire in the state semifinals. The Raiders came up heartbreakingly short, losing to Louisville St. Xavier in penalty kicks, 4-1, after a 1-1 draw Wednesday, Nov. 4. St. X advanced to the state championship game of the Kentucky High School Athletic Association boys soccer tournament after edging a scrappy Ryle team in the semifinals. Ryle finishes 17-4-1. St. X is 18-0-1. It is Ryle’s fifth loss in as many tries in the state semifinals in the last 10 years. “I'm really proud of this team,” said Ryle senior Damien Lakkis. “The last couple of years it hasn't worked for us. And this year I feel like we've been a family and we've worked for every single game, every single minute for each other. And the result wasn’t what we wanted, but we should be happy with ourselves because we worked our tails off.” “They played hard,” said head coach Stephen Collins. “Number two team in the country and I think we gave them all they could handle and that's all we could ask. It was a tough, hard-fought match and they played really well and I thought we played really well.” Collins was philosophical about the scheduling mixup by the KHSAA over the weekend. Ryle was supposed to play Dunbar in the semifinals but the KHSAA informed all the semifinalists Nov. 1 that the brackets they posted online didn’t match the official draw the association made before the tournament. The state finals are on a bigger field at the Lexington Soccer Club USL stadium. “I think they were a little upset, but as I told them, you're going to have to beat St. X to get a state title anyway,” Collins said. “You might as well play them first when you're healthy, you're rested, and it's a little bit smaller field. They're going to play 20 guys. Your best chance is to do it in game one and not when you play them on a bigger field when they got 20 guys.” Three keys to the game Ryle's tough defense : Ryle’s senior-led team worked together to keep the Tigers from getting easy scoring opportunities. St. X got its share of action, posting 19 total shots, eight on goal. Collins said the main keys were to stay focused because St. X’s top offensive players moved around the field a lot, and keeping them from getting into the corners and getting off dangerous crosses. “We saw that they moved guys back and forth across the field and so we talked to our guys about following them until they could switch with another player and making sure we weren't leaving them open,” Collins said. “They still got some guys open. They are phenomenal at moving into space and finding the open holes. “I think we figured it out eventually,” Lakkis said. “Everyone gives the credit to the defense, but it's really the whole team together. We work together as a team.” Confidence : St. Xavier scored two minutes into the game to lead 1-0, but the Raiders were never rattled. item.title: Three California sumo wrestlers added to World Elite Sumo Tournament in Orlando on Nov. 21
item.description: Professional wrestling star and sumo veteran, “Juicy Finau” (left), a massive, 6-foot-4, 465-pound competitor, will return to action at the World Elite Sumo event in Orlando on Saturday, Nov. 21. California will be well represented when World Elite Sumo (WES) returns to Orlando, Florida, later this month. Three California-based competitors—professional wrestler Juicy Finau of Chino, Josh "Siua" Tuitupou of Union City and Gilberto "El Coloso Aztec" De La Torre of Los Angeles—were among seven additional wrestlers announced Wednesday for WES' one-night, 12-man, open-weight tournament at Caribe Royale Orlando on Saturday, Nov. 21. The trio joins previously announced California competitor Makini "Big Mak" Manu of Carson, bringing the state's representation to four wrestlers. Finau, 30, is one of the largest competitors in the tournament, standing 6-foot-4 and weighing 465 pounds. The son of parents from the Kingdom of Tonga, Finau has five years of experience in Greco-Roman and freestyle wrestling, along with a professional wrestling career that has included appearances for AAA Lucha Libre and Major League Wrestling. Finau is also familiar with WES competition, having participated in the organization's Sept. 26 tournament in Santa Cruz, California, where he faced Manu in a matchup between two competitors weighing a combined 865 pounds. Tuitupou, meanwhile, returns to WES competition with a background in Muay Thai. The Union City wrestler, who weighs 268 pounds, utilizes a sumo style that emphasizes pushing, thrusting and disrupting his opponent's balance. De La Torre, a 400-pound competitor from Los Angeles, brings considerable sumo experience to Orlando. A three-time member of the United States national sumo team, De La Torre is known for his aggressive, forward-pressure style and his ability to establish a right-hand-inside grip on opponents. The three Californians will join Manu, the No. 1-ranked super heavyweight in Dana White's Power Slap organization. The 32-year-old Manu, a former professional football player who stands 6 feet tall and weighs 400 pounds, made his professional sumo debut at WES' Santa Cruz tournament in September. He defeated Finau in his opening matchup, winning two consecutive rounds in the best-of-three contest. The four California wrestlers will face a tournament field featuring competitors with backgrounds in mixed martial arts, Brazilian jiu-jitsu, collegiate wrestling and professional sumo. Other newly announced entrants include Florida competitors Brian Dina and Duke "The Viking" Webb, former collegiate wrestling national champion Jahsua Marsh of New York and returning WES competitor Rui Jr. of Brazil. Previously announced participants include reigning tournament champion Hidenoumi "The Iron Wall" Takuya of Japan and Orlando-based Soslan "Big Bear" Gagloev. WES also announced that Brennen Moorefield and Jakob "Mosin" Alekseyev have withdrawn from the tournament, with Moorefield sidelined by a training injury.

Kurth has spent most of his 32-year teaching and coaching career in Groton, including the past 30 years as an assistant coach and defensive coordinator for the Tigers. item.title: Calvary Day flag football team beats Woodville-Tompkins to win area title
item.description: The Calvary Day flag football team passed another regular season test with flying colors as the Cavs rolled to a 20-0 win over Woodville-Tompkins to win the Division I Area 3 championship at Islands Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 4th. Nick Grassi's squad was firing on all cylinders once again with an explosive offense led by junior quarterback Page Stewart and a stingy defense that recorded its 11th shutout of the season. The Cavs improved to 16-1 and 8-0 in Area play. Calvary will close out the regular season with non-region games against Richmond Hill, Southeast Bulloch and Bradwell Institute as it prepares for the Division I state playoffs where the Cavs will face an opponent to be determined on Nov. 18. Stewart entered the game with 3,211 yards passing with 58 touchdown passes and 13 interceptions and she wasted not time adding to her season stats. The junior connected with Rily Grassi for a 30-yard scoring strike on the Cavs first possession and later connected with Makayla Modicue ― hitting the senior in stride down the right sideline for a 50-yard touchdown. She later found Sanai Williams for a touchdown pass. Modicue had an interception on the first play from scrimmage after her touchdown and Kylie Singleton preserved the shutout in the second half with an interception in the end zone. Stewart hit a career milestone in the fourth quarter as she reached 10,000 yards passing for her career. "I have to credit my receivers for reaching that mark, 100% it all goes to them," Stewart said. "They run the routes, catch the passes and make the touchdowns, and that makes my job so much easier." It was the first Area title for the Cavs since 2023. Calvary reached the Division 2 state quarterfinals last year where the Cavs lost to eventual state champion Greenbrier and coach Nick Grassi thinks his squad has the firepower for another deep run. "It was great to see Page reach that mark tonight," Grassi said. "She is always so level headed ― she never gets too high or too low and that's what our team needs. If we keep playing with this kind of momentum, we should accomplish our goal and that's nothing short of playing in the Dome (for the state championship)." item.title: Dodgers Legend Hideo Nomo Set to Receive Prestigious Honor
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers icon Hideo Nomo will receive the inaugural Hall of Fame Sports Pioneer Medal at the 22nd Asian Hall of Fame induction ceremony in Los Angeles on Nov. 5. Asian Hall of Fame is a cultural, educational and research institution established in 2004 which “advances Asian and Native legacy to promote cross-cultural collaboration, strengthen interracial synergy, and inspire achievement across communities.” Former Los Angeles Dodgers president Peter O’Malley, who headed the team from 1970-1998 , will present the award to Nomo at the ceremony. “Asian Hall of Fame proudly honors Hideo Nomo (Los Angeles Dodgers) as the inaugural recipient of the Hall of Fame Sports Pioneer Medal,” Asian Hall of Fame wrote via Facebook. “Hideo Nomo’s groundbreaking MLB career opened doors for generations of Japanese players and transformed the landscape of professional baseball.” Oct 27, 2025; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers former player Hideo Nomo throws the ceremonial first pitch before game three of the 2025 MLB World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Who is Hideo Nomo? Nomo is a baseball pioneer who became the first Japanese major leaguer to permanently relocate to MLB. He was the second-ever Japanese playing to play professionally in the big leagues, following the San Francisco Giants’ Masanori Murakami, but is credited for paving the way for Japanese players in MLB . Nomo made his debut with the Dodgers in 1995, and pitched in parts of seven seasons with the Dodgers while also featuring for the Boston Red Sox, Detroit Tigers, Milwaukee Brewers, Tampa Bay Devils Rays, New York Mets and Kansas City Royals. During his seven seasons in Los Angeles, Nomo made 191 starts while posting a 3.74 ERA, striking out an even 1,200 batters in 1,217.1 innings pitched. He threw one of his two no-hitters with the Dodgers, and earned his sole All-Star appearance during his rookie year with the team in 1995. Now, more than 30 years after his debut, Japanese-born players are a mainstay across the league—but especially with the Dodgers. LA has carved out a core of key players from the NPB , bringing in Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Roki Sasaki over from NPB and signing Shohei Ohtani as soon as he hit the free agency market. While Nomo is long retired, his legacy on the game and his importance to opening MLB’s doors to Japan more than warrant his reception of the Hall of Fame Sports Pioneer Medal.

item.title: Remember Dan vs. Dave? What kids can learn from Olympian's redemption
item.description: COLORADO SPRINGS, CO – Do you like Dan or Dave? Reebok wanted you to pick a side. It was early 1992, and the shoe company launched a bold campaign by putting two virtually unknown decathletes all over America's television screens, starting with the Super Bowl. “I'm unstoppable, but, uh oh, something happens,” say Dan O’Brien , the former American decathlete remembering how he was on top of the world heading into that summer. “I look back on it, and I understand why it happened and how it happened.” O’Brien, at the peak of his powers, stumbled at the Olympic trials. He didn’t make the U.S. team. While Dave Johnson went to Barcelona, Spain, O’Brien fled to his apartment in Moscow, Idaho. “You're just like, ‘How on earth did this happen?’” O’Brien says. “Because you put so much into it, and not just the time on the track, but you dream about it, you think about it. You obsess over it. And when it doesn't happen, then you're like, ‘OK, what am I doing wrong?’ And that's the moment that you personally have to take ownership.” It’s a story that hits home for many of us: We’re really good at something like a sport and then, we’re not, as we struggle or others catch up. What we do next can shape the rest of our lives. O’Brien, who found something more inside of himself after failing during two significant moments of his, went on to future glory at one of the Olympics' most arduous events. He spoke with USA TODAY Sports on the occasion of a new U.S. Olympic & Paralympic Museum exhibit here that was his idea and inspiration. “A Legacy of Victory: U.S. Olympic Decathletes,” which O'Brien helped design, highlights the legacy of U.S. Olympic decathletes, who have won 27 medals at it, and what it takes to compete across 10 events over two days. “The perseverance part, I think, was just natural for me,” says O’Brien, 60. “I lost a lot of Little League games. We lost in the (state) semifinals my senior year in high school football, and we were, by far, the best team. And when I saw other people broken down by failures, that's just when I got better.” He had help from a few significant coaches, who carefully guided O’Brien but then let him do the work to figure out his journey. However, the Grizzlies are currently missing a key player in their rotation in point Scotty Pippen Jr. who has been dealing with a back injury . Scotty Pippen Jr. was officially ruled out for the Grizzlies’ game against the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday due to the back injury. But Grizzlies head coach Tuomas Iisalo seemed optimistic about Pippen’s prognosis and potential timeline for a return , as per Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal. He is expected to be either day-to-day or week-to-week, and he has seemingly avoided a more serious injury. Pippen will have missed two consecutive games now after playing in the first five games of the season at just about 16 minutes per. item.description: El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) talks with coach Jim Harbaugh during training camp at The Bolt. EL SEGUNDO, Calif. — The Los Angeles Chargers entered the 2026 season with expectations of competing for a Super Bowl. With the Super Bowl scheduled to be played at SoFi Stadium, the hope was that the Chargers would have an opportunity to compete for a championship in their own building. Instead, their season has turned into a nightmare. Entering Week 9, the Chargers are sitting at 0-7, and their biggest concern is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: Justin Herbert is playing some of the worst football of his career. Through seven games, Herbert has thrown 10 interceptions, a troubling number for a quarterback who entered the season with expectations of leading this team on a deep playoff run. The turnovers have become part of a much larger offensive problem, one that doesn't appear to be getting any better. The Chargers' offense has gone 27 consecutive drives without scoring a touchdown. That is the longest such streak since the Miami Dolphins went 30 drives without a touchdown in 2024, also under offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. Herbert has five touchdowns and has been sacked 23 times. For an offense with Herbert under center, those numbers are difficult to comprehend. The offensive operation has looked stale, inconsistent and increasingly predictable. There hasn't been much evidence of meaningful improvement, and with the bye week already behind them, it seems unlikely that the Chargers will make any significant coaching changes. If the organization was considering a shake-up, the bye week would have been the most logical opportunity. Instead, head coach Jim Harbaugh continues to publicly defend his quarterback and his offensive staff. Jim Harbaugh responds to Quentin Lake's criticism of Justin Herbert The conversation surrounding Herbert took another turn after Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake made comments questioning the quarterback's decision-making after their 24-9 loss to the Rams last Sunday. item.description: In just one year, Will Stein has helped Kentucky Football reach heights never seen in Lexington before. The biggest indicator of this came during Tuesday’s debut of the College Football Playoff Selection Committee Rankings, which had Kentucky earning its highest ranking ever at No. 6 . We also cannot forget all of the good his predecessor, Mark Stoops, did in Lexington during his 13-year run as the program’s head coach. Those two have helped nearly vanquish the ‘Old Kentucky Football’ trope that plagued this program for far too long. But for all the good we’ve seen them accomplish, Old Kentucky Football hasn’t been fully eradicated just yet. And these Wildcats have a chance to end a major part of that dreaded trope: Beating a good Tennessee team. Huh? Surely Kentucky has done that against a program it’s played in 83 consecutive seasons Unfortunately, you have to go back quite a ways to find a year Kentucky actually beat a good Volunteers team. You probably remember how the Vols once owned a 26-game winning streak in this series, which finally ended in 2011. And while Tennessee has still owned this series since then, the Wildcats do have two other wins since then in 2017 and 2020. In fact, that 2020 win in Knoxville was over an 18th-ranked Tennessee squad that’s not too far from this week’s 13th-ranked Volunteers team. However, that Tennessee team turned out to be a disaster, finishing 3-7 before having the entire season vacated due to recruiting violations. Kentucky’s 2017 win wasn’t much better. Those Vols finished 4-8 and fired head coach Butch Jones just two weeks after losing in Lexington. The 2011 Tennessee team at least had a chance to make a bowl game. The Vols entered the regular-season finale matchup with Kentucky at 5-6 overall, but the Matt Roark-led Wildcats scored an improbable 10-7 victory to send Derek Dooley’s Vols home for the holidays at 5-7. That’s the last time Kentucky beat a Vols team that finished with a winning record. Ironically, that Kentucky team featured defensive end Matt Stein, the father of first-year head coach Will Stein . item.title: Mizzou Eli Drinkwitz Shuts Down Florida State Rumors
item.description: FAYETTEVILLE, ARKANSAS - OCTOBER 31: Head Coach Eli Drinkwitz of the Missouri Tigers looks at the camera in the rain before the game against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Fayetteville, Arkansas. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) Getty The Missouri Tigers are entering the toughest stretch of their season, which has already included three top-25 opponents, with two of them coming on the road. The last thing that Mizzou head coach Eli Drinkwitz wants in his building is distraction. He quickly dismissed any rumors of his connection to the Florida State job opening after Mike Norvell was fired on Sunday. “I’m not a candidate at Florida State,” Drinkwitz said in his presser on Tuesday. “Let’s clear that up.” Every coaching carousel season, rumors flurry that Drinkwitz could be a candidate for a top job elsewhere. Last season it was Penn State and Florida. This season, it begins with the first major opening in college football. Eli Drinkwitz Wants Distraction-Free Environment Ahead Of Texas The Tigers begin a three-week gauntlet this week with the Texas Longhorns coming to Columbia, Missouri, and Drinkwitz wants his team to have a distraction-free environment. Drinkwitz made an emphasis on focusing on Texa s and not any of the other distractions that come with a high profile job opening up. This same song and dance comes around at this point every season that a premier job opens in college football. Whether that is for Drinkwitz or another coach in a spot to make a jump to a major player in the Power 4. Drinkwitz has been committed to Missouri since he stepped on campus to become the head coach in 2020, and turned a lackluster Missouri program into a regular in the top 25. Missouri’s Final Stretch Provides Path To College Football Playoffs The Tigers debut in the College Football Playoff rankings at No. 18, with three top-10 teams remaining on their schedule. The next three weeks will determine where Missouri stands in contention for a potential playoff berth. First up in No. 7 Texas, which is an old Big 12 rivalry renewed and a Texas team that has already suffered a pair of disappointing defeats this season. Following that, the Tigers head to face No. 3 Georgia before returning home to battle an upstart No. 6 Kentucky. The Tigers will then wrap up their season with the Oklahoma Sooners in Columbia. Missouri sitting at two losses already on the season, will have take care of business on their road. They might be able to suffer just one more loss with their tough schedule, but any more than that and they are certainly out of the playoffs. With Drinkwitz shutting down all rumors of a potential move to Florida State, the Tigers can focus on the task at hand. Missouri will look to take this final month one game at a time and put themselves in the best position come Selection Sunday. item.title: Haaland eyes 'lots of things' Man City can improve after Leipzig win
item.description: Manchester City's Erling Haaland celebrates scoring his side's third goal during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between RB Leipzig and Manchester City at Red Bull Arena. (is associated with: «Haaland eyes 'lots of things' Man City can improve after Leipzig win») Robert Michael/dpa Erling Haaland called on Manchester City to become more ruthless after twice being pegged back before beating RB Leipzig 3-2 on Wednesday. Haaland scored a 78th-minute winner as City finally saw off the German side in their Champions League league phase clash at the Red Bull Arena. Haaland felt City should have been more aggressive and killed the game off much earlier. "I think we need to step up a little bit," the Norwegian told TNT Sports. "I think when we were 1-0, I think we needed to push forward a bit more to go at it, go for the second and then hopefully go for the third. "That's what we have to do as a club. We have to work on that." Asked what areas the team could improve, Haaland added: "I think keeping the ball, when to keep it, when to go, working together, both offensively, defensively. Lots of different things. "That's the good part, you can always get better, and there's always a new chance, and now there will be a new game in three days, so that's lovely." City led after a Castello Lukeba own goal before half-time but that was cancelled out early in the second period by Ridle Baku. Enzo Fernandez restored City's lead but the impressive Antonio Nusa equalized again for Leipzig. Haaland had a quiet night until arriving at the back post to slide in the winner from Elliot Anderson's superb ball. It was just his 13th touch of the game. He said: "It's not the most but what is the most important is I help the team to win, and I managed to do that, so I'm super happy." It was Haaland's 14th goal of the season and a 13th in nine career appearances against Leipzig for the former Borussia Dortmund striker. He said: "I think it's the most I've scored against a club because I've played so many times against them. "As well in the Champions League with City every year I was in Dortmund as well. Leipzig are a good team, so I'm super happy about that." Manager Enzo Maresca was pleased with his players' response after Saturday's loss to Brighton, which was their second in succession in the Premier League. Maresca said: "I'm happy with the win. That is important, especially after a defeat. "I think part of the game we controlled quite well, creating many chances. Then for some moments, we struggled a little bit but that's normal, it's a Champions League game. It's Germany away. "It's always difficult, so we're happy with the win."
